intro: New Mexico runs elections county by county, through each county clerk, with the Secretary of State overseeing the state.

id_rule.text: You do not have to show ID to vote in a statewide election. You are asked to state your name, year of birth, and address. A first-time voter who registered by mail without ID has to show a physical ID.

elections.name: General election
elections.what: Federal, state and local offices, plus any statewide or local measures. Your exact ballot depends on where you live.

dates.label: Last day to register by mail, through an agent, or online
dates.detail: After this day, you can still register in person at your county clerk's office or an early voting site. Same-day registration is available through Election Day.

src.label: New Mexico Secretary of State, 2026 general election important dates

dates.label: Early voting
dates.detail: Early voting starts at county clerk offices on Oct. 6. More early voting sites open in many counties on Oct. 17. Early voting ends Oct. 31. Check with your county clerk for sites and hours.

src.label: New Mexico Secretary of State, 2026 general election important dates

dates.label: Last day to request a mailed ballot
dates.detail: Ask on NMVote.org, or use a paper application from the Secretary of State's website or your county clerk.

src.label: New Mexico Secretary of State, 2026 general election important dates

dates.label: Election Day
dates.detail: Polls are open 7 am to 7 pm. A mailed ballot must be received by 7 pm.
